clue.text: After overthrow, island guard is likely to be abolished

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, so the island and the guard are read backwards together

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
to cover is to guard or protect

explanation.surface: Once the regime falls, the island's protective force is probably going to be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator turns both pieces at once, so the island comes out last as ABLE. 'overthrow' suggests a coup, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revocable can be cancelled or withdrawn, so it may well be abolished.

clue.text: Last words of female con

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the closing inscription on a gravestone
taken as written

explanation.surface: The final statement of a woman convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' looks like a convict to match the surface, but it is the definition as a noun meaning a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is a swindle, and a rip-off is an informal word for a fraudulent overcharge.

clue.text: See most of Panorama, its content's current

indicators.note: what the shortened panorama holds is the next piece, placed inside it
only most of the word for a panorama is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a vista is a wide view or panorama
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Watch nearly all of a TV documentary, since its subject matter is topical.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the end of VISTA leaves VIST; 'its content's' puts I inside it. 'Panorama' suggests the BBC programme, but it just means a view.
explanation.definitionFit: To see someone, as in seeing a doctor, is to visit them.

clue.text: Revolutionary goes to English coastal town during strange, varied life

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal crossword revolutionary

indicators.note: the town and the abbreviation sit within the word for strange

parts.note: queer in its older sense means odd or strange
Redcar is a seaside town in north-east England

explanation.surface: A rebel travels to an English seaside town in the middle of an odd and eventful life story.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcar is a resort on England's north-east coast. The town and E go in after the first three letters of the strange word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered career is a working life with many ups and downs, so a varied history.

clue.text: Top musician wouldn't allow Mahler works to be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the words are given by their sound

parts.note: wouldn't allow suggests banned, and Mahler's works include Lieder, German art songs

explanation.surface: A leading conductor refuses to let Mahler's compositions go out on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: BANNED sounds like BAND and LIEDER, German songs such as Mahler wrote, sounds like LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandleader is the musician at the head of a band, so the top player.

clue.text: Language writer seldom uses

indicators.note: the run of letters is employed within the two words, sitting across their join

explanation.surface: A tongue that an author rarely employs.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are found across 'writER SEldom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: One sailor accommodated by another over in N African capital

indicators.note: the first sailor is housed inside the second one
over signals that the second sailor's word is turned round

parts.note: another sailor, and a tar is a seaman
AB, able-bodied seaman, is one sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is given a berth by a shipmate in a North African city.
explanation.walkthrough: AB and TAR are both standard crossword sailors; 'over' turns only the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Holding breath, poorly old man's to sample something prepared in bakery

parts.note: feeling rough means feeling poorly
a puff is a short breath
pa is father, the old man, with the possessive S
to try is to taste or sample

explanation.surface: Struggling for breath while unwell, Dad gets to taste something from the baker's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' is a link here: the pieces just run side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough puff pastry is a quick flaky dough a baker makes for pies and sausage rolls.

clue.text: Lawyer's deal involves endless gamble

indicators.note: the word for a deal surrounds the shortened gamble

parts.note: to barter is to trade or deal

indicators.note: the last letter of the gamble word is cut off

parts.note: a risk is a gamble

explanation.surface: A solicitor's agreement includes a never-ending wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawyer's' reads as possessive, but the 's is just 'is' linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who argues cases in the higher courts of Britain.

clue.text: During stay you will be fed second-rate fruit

indicators.note: the next piece lies within the word for stay

parts.note: to tarry is to stay or linger

indicators.note: the old word for you takes the grade letter into its middle

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
B is a second-class grade

explanation.surface: While you are visiting you will be served poor-quality fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-rate' gives B, as in a B grade, which the old word for you takes in before both go inside the stay word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tayberry is a cross between a raspberry and a blackberry, a kind of soft berry.

clue.text: Bill's name stuck on back door

indicators.note: the name abbreviation is attached to the end of the bill word

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster

explanation.surface: A man's handbill has a name pasted on the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck on' fits a poster on a door, but it is only telling you to add N.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear or side gate, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Plant prolific initially in part of southern Britain

indicators.note: the initial letter is placed within the county name

parts.note: Surrey is a county south of London

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word prolific is used

explanation.surface: A vigorously spreading plant found in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY is a county in southern England; P goes inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurrey is a small weed of the pink family with white flowers.

clue.text: Be integrated every now and then

definitions.meaning: to ... is to be wholly integrated, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to fit in completely; as one word it means intermittently, by fits and starts.

clue.text: Bird disturbed by hikers

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird is upset by walkers on the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrike is a songbird that impales prey on thorns, also called a butcher-bird.

clue.text: Alcohol in small amount has grip on Mexican, but not me

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the small amount holds the shortened Mexican inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of drink

indicators.note: the letters of the word me are taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Mexican has a firm hold on a small measure of liquor, though I don't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not me' takes ME away from MEXICAN, leaving XICAN for the small measure to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoxicant is any substance that makes one drunk, alcohol being the usual example.

clue.text: Who might be unearthing rubbish on counter?

definitions.text: Who might be unearthing rubbish on counter?

indicators.note: in an across clue the shuffled letters follow the counter word, placed on it

parts.note: a bar is a counter in a pub or shop

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone rummaging through junk piled on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' looks like the thing being dug up, but it signals that the letters of 'unearthing' are rearranged, giving GAINHUNTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper who seeks out cheap deals is hunting for bargains on sale tables.

clue.text: Actress in Swiss location having tough time

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital
hard means tough

explanation.surface: A performer in a Swiss city having a difficult spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Bernhardt was a celebrated French stage performer of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: Drink wife's consumed during most of tea party, surprisingly

indicators.note: the wife is taken in amid the jumbled letters
surprisingly signals the letters come out in an unexpected order
all but the last letter of tea party is used

explanation.surface: My wife drank something during almost all of the tea party, which was unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA PART, without the Y, is rearranged by 'surprisingly' to TAPATER, and W goes in after TAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the mains is something to drink.

clue.text: Film cut a great deal, circulated after receiving two Oscars

parts.note: to abridge is to shorten or cut

indicators.note: the great deal word takes the two letters into it
circulated means sent round, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a raft of things is a great many
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet, so two of them give OO

explanation.surface: A movie was heavily edited, then shown around after winning two Academy Awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a raft of' means a great deal of. After the two O's go in, 'circulated' turns the result round to give TOOFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bridge Too Far is a 1977 war movie about the Arnhem operation of 1944.

clue.text: Film maker gushes as broadcast …

indicators.note: broadcast means heard over the airwaves, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: wells as a verb means gushes or springs up

explanation.surface: A director goes on effusively when on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane, so he was a movie maker.

clue.text: This musical sound repulsed wartime broadcaster

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Lord Haw-Haw was the nickname of William Joyce, who broadcast Nazi propaganda to Britain

explanation.surface: This sound of music disgusted a propagandist on the wartime radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Haw-Haw broadcast Nazi propaganda to Britain in the Second World War; 'repulsed' turns his name round.
explanation.definitionFit: Wah-wah is the wavering effect a guitar pedal or trumpet mute gives a note.

clue.text: Italian meal's cooked with wine — no starter needed

indicators.note: cooked means prepared, and here it means the letters are worked over

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

indicators.note: the first letter of the word wine is removed

explanation.surface: An Italian dish is prepared with wine, and no appetiser is required.
explanation.walkthrough: WINE loses its first letter to give INE; with MEALS it makes the pool rearranged by 'cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milanese describes a person or thing from Milan, a city in Italy.

clue.text: … goes out live, after final tweak

indicators.note: the closing letters of the word for live are adjusted, one shifted past its neighbour

parts.note: to exist is to live

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the film-maker departs on air after a last adjustment.
explanation.walkthrough: EXIST has its T moved before the S. The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits as a verb means leaves or departs.

clue.text: Teacher supervises first part of examination as agreed

indicators.note: in a down clue the teacher sits above the next letter, as one watching over it

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word examination is used

explanation.surface: A lecturer invigilates the start of a test as arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Done, as in 'It's a deal, done!', means settled or agreed.

clue.text: Poor Ted, doddery wreck

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Poor old Ted is a shaky wreck of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' looks like a noun describing Ted, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to wreck it.

clue.text: Scene of great activity giving you an exciting experience right away

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for right is sent away from the thrill word

parts.note: a thrill is an exciting experience

explanation.surface: Something that gives you a buzz straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately', but it tells you to take R out of THRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ant colony's mound is a byword for busy industry.

clue.text: Turner runs over hill

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: The painter Turner dashes across a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but it means something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the revolving part of a machine, so it is something that turns.

clue.text: Francois Hollande's in meetings about independent, subversive politicians

parts.note: the former French president would say en for in

indicators.note: the meetings word goes around the abbreviation for independent

parts.note: trysts are secret meetings

explanation.surface: The French president takes part in discussions on an independent candidate and radical politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollande was president of France, so his word for 'in' is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: Entryists join a party to subvert it from within, a tactic of hard-left groups.
